leak_found_2.what: The deployed Supabase Auth config named only dead predecessor hosts (site_url on the retired product domain, allow-list on the retired deployment), so the consent page on the live domain got 400 'unauthorized request origin' and pairing died at the approval step - the funnel's wall between 15 pair views and 1 install view.
leak_found_2.proof: owner console capture 2026-11-24 (the oauth consent endpoint answered 400 unauthorized request origin); CI read run 45373897531 printed the predecessor site_url and an allow-list without navego.pages.dev.
leak_found_2.fix: CI workflow .github/workflows/auth-config.yml (PRs #436, #437, #438, #439) patched production: site_url=https://navego.pages.dev and uri_allow_list gained https://navego.pages.dev/*, verified from run 45376655642 log; pinned by decisions.json -> hosted-consent-origin-01.

paypal_revenue_gap.what: A completed PayPal order activated a Navego plan but wrote no settled sale, so a real payment could leave the economy ledger and the automation score unchanged.
paypal_revenue_gap.proof: live production query 2026-11-24: opera_price_orders held 0 rows, opera_notification_log held only Midtrans sandbox events, and opera_plan_activate_purchase changed plans without recording a PayPal order.
paypal_revenue_gap.fix: hosted/migrations/20261125000000_opera_paypal_orders.sql owns the quote, one-sale claim, and one activation; hosted/migrations/20261125010000_opera_paypal_orders_hardening.sql separates quoted and actual values, normalizes the lock key, and makes the accepted revenue event unique. Both migrations and navego-billing were deployed on 2026-11-24 in runs 45461731759 and 45469501568. Pinned by decisions.json -> hosted-paypal-revenue-01; decisions.json -> hosted-paypal-revenue-02.

install_path_fix.what: The download page promised a one-command install but put the manual zip download first, and the anonymous landing page sent a visitor through a second page before they could install; the live funnel had 62 landing-page views from 60 browsers against 5 download-page views from 2 browsers and no install click.
install_path_fix.proof: Before the landing change, live production had 142 page views, 68 pair views, 5 install views, 0 install clicks, and 0 settled orders. After PR #453 deployed in run 45533243742, a production 320px Chrome drive with the funnel endpoint blocked found the exact command visible, the force-install cost and undo disclosure above the button, the button fully above the consent banner, copy success announced, later failure unable to hide it, and focus still on the retryable button. The live install surface has not yet recorded a real landing view or click; synthetic proof events were blocked rather than presented as customer intent.
install_path_fix.fix: site/app/components/CopyCommand.tsx owns the one copy control, site/app/routes/index.tsx carries the Windows command in the anonymous landing hero, and site/app/routes/unduh.tsx keeps it on the download page. site/app/lib/funnel.ts records one gated install.view per landing session and a successful copy as install.click with surface landing or download. PRs #446-#453 were deployed in runs 45491328739, 45496998537, 45500375491, 45503586044, 45506819246, and 45533243742. Pinned by decisions.json -> site-install-cta-01 and site-install-cta-02.
